item.title: Opt-in Linux 7.3 Kernel for Proxmox VE 9 available
item.author: invalid@example.com (t.lamprecht)
item.dc:creator: t.lamprecht
item.content:encoded:
We recently uploaded the 7.3 kernel to the test and no-subscription repositories of all our Debian Trixie-based releases. It will stay an opt-in kernel for these release series, while the 7.0-based kernel remains the default for them.

Unlike our previous kernels, which were based on the Ubuntu kernel, the 7.3 kernel is based directly on the upstream stable branch from kernel.org. 7.3 is also likely to become this year's upstream longterm (LTS) kernel.

item.title: The case for BCacheFS inclusion in PVE
item.author: invalid@example.com (alexskysilk)
item.dc:creator: alexskysilk
item.content:encoded:
PVE has (and continues to have) a large presence in the homelab/self hosting crowd. The Primary filesystem option employed for single host applications was and is ZFS, due to its robust featureset and code maturity. Yet ZFS's core structural geometry—fixed virtual device (vdev) layouts, rigid pool topologies, and bolt-on workarounds like RAIDZ expansion or special vdevs—shows strain when modern single-node servers mix NVMe, SATA SSDs, and high-capacity hard drives.
